Attention-Based Retrieval for Multi-Hop Question Answering

Abstract
We study retrieval-augmented generation for multi-hop question answering. Our method scores candidate passages with a learned attention module and re-ranks them before generation. On HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA it improves exact match by 3.1 and 2.4 points over a strong dense-retrieval baseline, at a cost of 18% more inference time.

1 Introduction
Large language models answer many factual questions, but multi-hop questions require combining evidence from several documents. Retrieval systems that score each passage independently often miss the bridge entity that links two hops. We propose a re-ranker that attends over the full candidate set.

2 Related Work
Dense passage retrieval (Karpukhin et al., 2020) encodes questions and passages separately. Fusion-in-decoder (Izacard and Grave, 2021) reads many passages at once. Our approach sits between the two.

3 Method
Given a question q and candidates p1..pk, we compute attention weights over all candidates and select the top m for the generator. Training uses a contrastive loss with hard negatives mined from the baseline retriever.

4 Experiments
We train for 40,000 steps with batch size 64 on 8 GPUs. The total compute budget was approximately $2,300 of cloud time. Results are averaged over three seeds; standard deviations are below 0.4 points.

5 Results
Table 2 shows exact match and F1. The re-ranker helps most on bridge questions, where the second hop depends on an entity named only in the first passage.

6 Conclusion
Attending over the candidate set is a cheap way to improve multi-hop retrieval. Future work includes extending the method to conversational settings.

References
Izacard, G. and Grave, E. (2021). Leveraging passage retrieval with generative models.
Karpukhin, V. et al. (2020). Dense passage retrieval for open-domain question answering.
